title: Poached Eggs on Buttered Sourdough Toast with Chives
summary: Very fresh eggs, drained of their thin whites, are poached in barely simmering water until the yolks are set, then served on buttered sourdough with chives.
equipment: wide saucepan or casserole (about 24 cm, at least 2.5 litres)

steps.title: Heat the water
steps.text: Bring the water to the boil in the wide pan, then lower the heat until it barely shivers, with small bubbles on the base (about 90 °C). Gentle heat cooks the white evenly without tearing it apart.

steps.title: Drain the eggs
steps.text: Crack one egg into the sieve set over the small bowl and swirl for 20-30 seconds so the thin, watery white drips away, then tip the egg into a ramekin. Repeat with each egg. Removing the loose white is what stops ragged wisps forming in the pan.

steps.title: Poach
steps.text: Hold a ramekin just above the water and gently tip in the egg, then repeat with the others, spacing them apart. Keep the water at a bare simmer and cook for 6-7 minutes, until the whites are firm and the yolk feels firm when pressed with a spoon (71 °C at the centre). Set yolks need a few minutes longer than runny ones.

steps.title: Toast the bread
steps.text: Meanwhile, toast the bread and spread it with the butter. Thick, well-toasted sourdough holds the eggs without going soggy.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Lift each egg with the slotted spoon, rest it on kitchen paper for a moment to drain, then set 2 on each toast. Scatter with chives, salt and pepper and serve.

tips: Fresh eggs give the neatest shape, because their whites are thicker.
A rolling boil is the commonest mistake: it breaks up the whites, so keep the water just shivering.
Use a wide pan so the eggs do not touch.
Blot each egg on kitchen paper before plating so the toast stays crisp.
storage: Best eaten straight away. Poached eggs can be chilled in cold water for up to 1 day and reheated in hot water until piping hot. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
